programs.name: excavate-turtle
programs.title: Excavator
programs.tagline: Digs a hole of any size and walls it in so no water or lava gets inside, ready for the builder turtles to fill. Or exactly the hole a building plan needs.
features: Digs any size of hole: up, down, or deep under a shaft
Walks every wall, floor and ceiling block and fills caves, water and lava with cobblestone
Leaves the inside empty: inner walls and details are for the builder turtle
Deep mode digs a shaft down (sealed too) and digs the hole 10 above bedrock

excavate <plan> digs the hole an underground plan asks for (bunker, cellar, hideout, workshop, burrow, cloister, greathall, crossroads, sanctum, atrium, grandstair, fortress, cavern, deephold) and prints where the builder goes and the build command
Resumes after reboots, chunk unloads, or being picked up
With a storage system: its chest on the storage cable (or an ender chest twin of one) sends the loot home and gets fuel and cobblestone ordered into it
setup: Place the turtle at floor level in one corner of the hole-to-be. The hole grows forward and to the right.
Put a chest directly behind it with some coal in. Loot goes in there too. With a storage computer, make it a chest on the storage cable, or an ender chest whose twin is.
Run the command. It prints the size and the fuel it needs, then gets to work.
commands: 21×21×16 hole, digging up from the turtle
shaft down, hole floor 10 above bedrock
a 30×30×30 cube centred under the turtle, floor 10 above bedrock
the 17×17×7 hole for the cellar plan; any plan name works
a job from before GPS was needed: you put it back on its start block
integrates: Shows its progress, position and fuel on the dashboard.
Needs GPS: it checks its position every 20 steps and finds its way back if moved.
Its chest can be one on the storage cable (or an ender chest twin of one): it claims it as its delivery chest, so the loot it leaves goes home, and orders coal and cobblestone into it when short.

Builds whatever goes inside the hole from a plan sent by build control or the projector: inner walls, decorative walls and details. After excavate <plan>, that plan: any of the fourteen underground plans, from the bunker to the deep hold.

render.caption: Cut-away of the default hole: empty, with cobblestone where it sealed caves in the walls and floor.

programs.name: strip-mine-turtle
programs.title: Strip Miner
programs.tagline: A 3×3 main tunnel with 3×3 branches off both sides, at any depth, torches every 8 blocks, loot hauled home.
features: Throws junk away and only brings back the good stuff
Mines deep: 'at -54' digs a shaft down first and hauls everything back up it
Places torches from its inventory as it goes
Never digs chests, spawners or ComputerCraft blocks
Refuels from the chest, including coal it mined itself
setup: Place the turtle on the floor where the tunnel starts, facing the way to dig.
Put a chest directly behind it with some coal in.
Optional: give it torches. Run the command and press Enter.
commands: a shaft down to Y -54 first, then the tunnels down there
a job from before GPS was needed: you put it back on its start block
integrates: Reports what it's digging and how far along it is.
Needs GPS: it keeps it on route if it gets moved.

render.caption: A smaller strip mine being dug: main tunnel first, each pair of branches as it passes them.

lines: GPS found: I'll check my position as I go.

programs.name: nether-tunnel-turtle
programs.title: Nether Tunnel
programs.tagline: A sealed 3×3 tunnel through the Nether: holes patched, lava walled off or scooped up for fuel.
features: Patches holes in the walls, floor and ceiling: caves, ravines, open air over lava lakes
Walls off lava beside the tunnel and fills in lava in the way, so none gets in
Scoops up lava sources with a bucket and burns them for fuel
Replaces gravel, fire and plants in the walls with solid blocks
Throws junk away, keeps 128 patch blocks, brings the loot home
setup: Place the turtle on the floor where the tunnel starts, facing the way to dig.
Put a chest directly behind it with some coal in, and a few stacks of cobblestone for stronger walls.
Optional: give it an empty bucket and torches. Run the command and press Enter.
commands: a job from before GPS was needed: you put it back on its start block
integrates: Reports how far along the tunnel it is.
Needs GPS: it keeps it on route if it gets moved.

render.caption: A shorter tunnel being dug through netherrack: a cave wall patched, a sealed bridge over a lava lake, a lava pocket walled off.

lines: GPS found: I'll check my position as I go.
Needs about 1536 fuel (have 1200). I refuel from the chest
behind me, so put coal in it.
I'll scoop up lava with my bucket and burn it.
Patch blocks on board: 128. I use netherrack I dig, but
Chest goes directly behind me. Press Enter to start.

programs.name: level-turtle
programs.title: Land Leveller
programs.tagline: Flattens an area into a solid building platform: cuts down hills and trees, fills dips, ponds and holes with the dirt it dug.
features: The platform's height is the ground the turtle starts on
Cuts away everything above it in 3-high layers: hills, whole trees, leaves, grass, snow
With no height given, keeps going up until the sky is clear (up to 64)
Fills dips, ponds and holes below it with the dirt and stone it dug, up to 8 deep; deeper caves get an 8-block plug
Wood and loot go in the chest; spare dirt too, and it takes it back out when it needs more
Never burns the wood it chops; resumes after reboots, chunk unloads, or being picked up
setup: Stand the turtle on the ground in one corner of the area, at the height you want the platform, facing along one edge. The area runs forward and to the right.
Put a chest directly behind it with some coal in. Wood and loot go in there too.
Run the command. It prints the size and the fuel it needs, then gets to work.
commands: 32 to the right, 32 forward, cleared up until the sky is empty
clear nothing above, only fill the holes below
a job from before GPS was needed: you put it back on its start block
integrates: Shows its progress, position and fuel on the dashboard.
Needs GPS: it checks its position every 20 steps and finds its way back if moved.
Once the platform is down, send a plan to the builder turtles at its corner.

render.caption: A finished platform in rolling land: hills cut down to it, dips and the pond filled with dirt and cobblestone, trees outside left alone.

lines: GPS found: I'll check my position as I go.
Platform 32x32, clearing up until the sky is clear.
Holes below get filled, up to 8 deep.
Needs about 6476 fuel (have 5000). I refuel from the chest
behind me, so put coal in it. Wood goes there too.
Chest goes directly behind me. Press Enter to start.

programs.name: village-turtle
programs.title: Village Builder
programs.tagline: Builds a themed village outward from a plaza, choosing each building to suit the ground, with paved, lit streets.
features: Medieval, desert, nordic and japanese themes
Starts by building a depot round itself and its chests
Surveys each plot and picks a building that fits the terrain
Streets with curbs, lamp posts and stairs on slopes
Saves after every block: survives any number of reboots
Build with a crew: with GPS, more village turtles join and take plots of their own
Optional: fetches blocks from the storage system and shows its next building on the projector
setup: Stand the turtle on fairly flat ground at the village centre, facing the village's "forward".
Supply chest directly behind it (a double chest is best), spoil chest to its left. With a storage system, put a wired modem on the supply chest, on the storage cable: the turtle hooks it up itself.
Fill the supply chest. 'village list medieval' shows what each building needs. Best with a big barrel: an empty buffer chest under the turtle.
Run 'village', pick a theme and a radius.
commands: let a finished village grow further
a village from before GPS was needed: reset to its home block
help another village turtle build its village, from this turtle's own chests (GPS)
integrates: Shows the plot it's on, and exactly which blocks it's waiting for.
Needs GPS: it checks itself every 25 blocks and recalibrates if moved.
With a wireless modem, 'projector village' shows the building it's working on, right on its plot.
Counts what's in the storage system and has it sent to the supply chest as each load is needed.
Blocks that can be crafted from what's stored count as available, and get made when it asks.

render.caption: Rendered from the real blueprints and from a 12-building village built in the simulator. Setup shows where the turtle and its chests go.

lines: 1) Medieval: timber frame, cobble, spruce roofs
2) Desert: sandstone, flat roofs, open doorways
3) Nordic: spruce longhouses, steep dark roofs
4) Japanese: dark wood, pale walls, tiled hip roofs
Medieval village, up to 48 blocks out (about 21 plots).

programs.name: mob-farm-turtle
programs.title: Mob Farm Builder
programs.tagline: Builds a classic drop-tower mob farm: dark spawning room, water channels, drop shaft and collection chest.
features: Default drop kills everything; loot collects in the chest
XP mode leaves mobs on half a heart at a kill window
2-block headroom keeps endermen out
Builds with any block you put in slot 1
setup: Pick a spot with open sky. Over an ocean or far from caves works best.
Place the turtle where you want to stand to collect, facing the way the farm should go.
Supply chest directly behind it. 'mobfarm list' shows what goes in it. Best with a big barrel: an empty buffer chest under the turtle.
Run the command and press Enter.
commands: XP farm: mobs land on half a heart
what to put in the chest
a job from before GPS was needed: you put it back on its start block
integrates: Shows which part of the farm it's building and what it's waiting for.
Needs GPS: the same position checks as the excavator.

render.caption: The default farm: finished, cut open, and a close-up of the bottom of the shaft. Setup shows where the turtle and its chests go before it starts.

lines: GPS found: I'll check my position as I go.
Mob farm with a 32 block drop: 18x18 spawning room 32 blocks up,
high enough to kill everything that falls.
Needs about 2000 fuel (have 900); I refuel from the chest.
Chest goes directly behind me. Press Enter to start.

programs.name: tree-farm-turtle
programs.title: Tree Farm
programs.tagline: Plants a grid of saplings, chops each tree as it grows, replants it and hauls the logs to a chest. For ever.
features: Walks lanes beside the trees, never through them
Picks up saplings and apples that drop from the leaves
Uses bone meal on young saplings if you give it some
Burns some of its logs when fuel runs low, so it runs itself
setup: Clear a flat patch of dirt or grass at least 11 × 18.
Place the turtle at the near left corner, facing along the farm. Chest directly behind it.
Give it saplings, some coal and any bone meal. Run the command and press Enter.
commands: a job from before GPS was needed: you put it back on its start block
stop farming and forget the farm
integrates: Shows which round and tree it's on, and how many logs so far.
Make its chest the storage system's input and the logs get put away.
Needs GPS: it keeps it on the farm if it gets moved.

render.caption: The default farm part way through a round: grown trees, fresh saplings, and one being chopped.

lines: GPS found: I'll check my position as I go.
24 trees in 4 columns of 6, 3 apart. The farm is 11 wide and 18 long.
I have 16 saplings; 24 would plant every spot.
Coal in my inventory stays there; I burn logs too when I'm low.
Chest goes directly behind me. Press Enter to start.

programs.name: crop-farm-turtle
programs.title: Crop Farm
programs.tagline: Flies over a field, harvests whatever is ripe, replants it from its own seeds and drops the harvest in a chest.
features: Wheat, carrots, potatoes, beetroot and nether wart, mixed any way
Only harvests fully grown crops and replants straight away
Picks melons and pumpkins, leaves the stems
Keeps a stack of each seed, the rest goes in the chest
setup: Place the turtle one block above a corner of the field, facing along one edge.
Put a chest directly behind it, at the same height.
Give it some coal. Run the command and press Enter.
commands: a job from before GPS was needed: you put it back on its start block
stop farming and forget the field
integrates: Shows its round, how far across the field it is and the harvest so far.
Make its chest the storage system's input and the harvest gets put away.

render.caption: A 9 × 9 field with water in the middle: harvested and replanted behind the turtle, ripe ahead of it.

lines: GPS found: I'll check my position as I go.
Field 9 wide and 9 long, starting under me. About 99 fuel a round.
I fly one block above the crops, so keep that layer clear.
Coal in my inventory stays there. Chest goes directly behind me.

programs.name: cobble-breeder
programs.title: Cobblemon Breeder
programs.tagline: Breeds better and better Pokémon from a Cobbreeding pasture: reads every egg's IVs before it hatches, sends the better ones to the incubator and tells you which breeder to swap, on the way to a 6x31.
features: Reads each egg's IVs, nature and gender in the egg chest, before it hatches
An egg that beats the weakest breeder goes to the incubator; the rest to a reject chest, deleted or hatched
Says which breeder to recall and follows the pasture, so a swap never needs scanning
Monitor: every breeder's six IVs, progress to 6x31, the best of each stat and the last eggs
setup: Set eggEncryptionEnabled to false in config/cobbreeding/main.json and run /cobbreeding reload.
Put a hopper under the pasture into an egg chest, and a hopper on top of the incubator (keep the incubator away from the pasture).
Place a command computer within 8 blocks of them with a monitor, install, and run 'breed setup' to pick each chest.
Send each breeder out next to the computer and tap Scan (or type its IVs with 'breed ivs'), then put it in the pasture.
commands: find the pasture and chests around the computer and pick each
run it on the monitor (runs on boot once set up)
read the Pokémon sent out next to the computer
forget the egg history and the best egg
integrates: Shows the best breeder's progress, and turns yellow when a swap is waiting or a chest is full.

render.caption: The breeder on a monitor, with made-up eggs. When a better egg comes in, tap Make the swap to play your part.

programs.name: mine-server
programs.title: AutoMine Server
programs.tagline: The brain of AutoMine: hands chunks out to a fleet of mining turtles and shows a touch map for planning.
features: Queue chunks for turtles, or reserve some for yourself
Status board on any attached monitor
Pause sends every turtle home; resume sends them back
Turtles keep mining while the server is down
setup: Place an advanced computer with a modem, plus any monitors.
Reboot. The server starts on its own and restarts if it ever stops.
Place each miner where it should live, with its own chest right behind it: that spot is its home.
commands: drop every queued and in-progress chunk (Ctrl+T first, then reboot)
cruise height, depth, monitors, junk list
integrates: Every miner asks this server for its next chunk over rednet.
Reports job totals to the dashboard.

render.caption: The AutoMine touch map. Pick a tool and tap chunks to try it.

programs.name: mine-turtle
programs.title: AutoMine Turtle
programs.tagline: Same code on every miner. Asks the server for a chunk, flies there and mines it out, layer by layer.
features: Flies at its own cruise lane so miners don't collide
Drops junk as it goes, goes home to unload and refuel
Picks up where it stopped after a reboot
Waits at home, its own spot and chest, when there's nothing queued
setup: Craft a mining turtle with an ender modem (or wireless modem).
Place it, give it a bit of coal and run 'refuel all'.
Install and reboot. It names itself Miner-<id>.
It needs GPS to find its own position and facing (it steps forward once, so give it room in front).
Every miner: put its own chest right behind it, open sky above. That spot is its home: it unloads, refuels and waits there.
commands: make this spot my home (chest behind me), e.g. to move it
integrates: Gets jobs from the server; the server never mines a chunk with a miner's home in it.
Miners need GPS: it finds their position and facing and keeps them on track while mining.
Each miner shows up with its chunk, progress and fuel.

render.caption: Three chunks: one mined out, one in progress, one still queued.

programs.name: status-server
programs.title: Status Dashboard
programs.tagline: A live monitor wall of every computer and turtle: state, what it's doing, where it is and its fuel.
features: Colour-coded cards: working, idle, waiting, travelling, error
Tap a card for its details and recent activity
Shows GPS or tracked positions
Pages through big fleets
setup: Place an advanced computer with a modem and an advanced monitor.
Install and reboot. Anything running lib/report.lua shows up on its own.
integrates: Every program here reports to it through lib/report.lua.
Add two lines to any program of your own to put it on the dashboard.

render.caption: The dashboard on a 3×2 advanced monitor. It updates as computers report in.

programs.name: turtle-finder
programs.title: Turtle Finder
programs.deviceLabel: Pocket computer + wireless or ender modem
programs.tagline: Lost a turtle? Lists every turtle it hears, nearest first, and points a big arrow straight at the one you pick.
features: Every turtle heard, nearest first, with its distance and direction
A big arrow pointing the way you last walked, or a compass with north up
How far away, which direction, how far above or below you, and its coordinates
What it is doing: stuck, waiting, clearing, out of fuel
Green, yellow or red by how fresh its position is
Remembers where it last heard each one, even after you close it
setup: Put a wireless or ender modem on a pocket computer.
Install it, stand somewhere with GPS, and run finder.
Pick a turtle with the arrow keys and Enter, or run finder <name>.
Walk a few blocks the way you are looking, then open the pocket computer: the arrow points at the turtle.
commands: every turtle heard, nearest first; Enter follows one
follow the one whose label has that in it
list every computer, not just turtles
integrates: Every program that reports its status is findable: that message carries its GPS position.
Both you and the turtle need GPS for the arrow.
Listens to the same messages; the finder is the version you carry.

render.caption: On an advanced pocket computer: the list of turtles heard, then the arrow to a lost leveller.

programs.name: overseer-bridge
programs.title: Overseer
programs.deviceLabel: Computer + ender modem, and your PC
programs.tagline: A live map of your whole network in your browser: where every computer and turtle is, what it is doing, and every message flying between them.
features: Every computer and turtle on a map where it is, coloured by what it is doing
Messages fly between them as glowing streaks, coloured by protocol; broadcasts ripple out
Turtle trails, a searchable fleet list with fuel bars, and alerts for stuck or erroring machines
A traffic chart of the last two minutes and a live log of every message: who, to whom, what, how big
Click anything for its position, fuel, uptime, who it talks to and what it has been doing
A demo world plays when no server is running, so you can try the page right away
setup: On your PC, run node tools/overseer/server.mjs. It prints a key and the two set lines for the bridge.
Allow CC to reach your PC: add an [[http.rules]] allow rule for 127.0.0.1 port 8090 above the $private rule in computercraft-server.toml.
Place a computer with an ender modem (and a wired one for a cable you want to hear), install the bridge, and type the two set lines.
Type overseer test, reboot, and open http://localhost:8090.
commands: where the overseer server runs (it prints this)
check the server answers, and say what is wrong if it does not
run the bridge (startup.lua does this on boot)
on your PC: the server and the page
integrates: Every program that reports its status shows up on the map with its position, state and fuel.
The same reports, on a monitor in-game; the bridge itself shows on it too.
Its requests, deliveries and crafting messages are the busiest streaks on the map.
Watch the miners spread through their chunks and report back to the mine server.

render.caption: The overseer page in a browser: the map, the fleet, traffic and the packet stream. The real page is animated: try the demo. Setup shows where the bridge and its modems go.

lines: The overseer server answered. All good!
Reboot (or type 'overseer') to start the bridge.

programs.name: update-watcher
programs.title: Update Watcher
programs.tagline: Publish a new version and every computer in range picks it up: the watcher sees who is out of date and has each one update and reboot, one at a time.
features: Every computer sends the versions it has installed with its status report; the watcher compares them with the website
Out-of-date computers fetch the new files in the background and reboot, then carry on with their job
One at a time, so the base never goes down all at once; then it updates itself
A list on the terminal and an optional monitor: up to date, out of date, updating, no answer
updates auto off only shows what is behind, and U updates them when you are ready
set install.remote false on any computer it should leave alone
setup: Place a computer with a wireless modem (an ender modem reaches every computer with one, anywhere).
Optional: put a monitor next to it or on its cable.
Install it and reboot.
commands: run the watcher (startup.lua does this on boot)
update by itself, or only show what is out of date
how often to look at the website (default 2)
pick the monitor it shows the list on
on another computer: say no to the watcher
integrates: Sends each computer's installed versions and answers the watcher, so every program that reports its status can be updated.
Shows a computer as updating while it fetches the new files.
Answers the watcher from its own event loop.

render.caption: The watcher's screen: computers that need you first, then the ones up to date.

lines: It will only show what's out of date. Press U to update them.

programs.name: gps-deployer
programs.title: GPS Deployer
programs.tagline: Flies up and builds a working 4-computer GPS constellation, installs gps host on each and switches them on; optionally wraps each host in a satellite.
features: Finds the build limit itself, whatever the modpack
Hosts label themselves and restart gps host on boot
Optional satellites: a hull round each computer, antenna dish, solar wings and lights
Tests the new GPS when it lands
Re-run after a problem: finished hosts and blocks are skipped
setup: Load the turtle: 4 computers, 4 modems, a disk drive, a floppy disk and fuel (plus the satellite blocks for gps-deploy satellite).
Place it somewhere with open sky above it.
Run the command and enter its X, Y, Z and facing from F3.
commands: hosts spread wider, each built into a satellite
integrates: Every turtle here uses GPS to find and check its position.
Hosts appear on the dashboard as "gps host".

render.caption: The four hosts high above the start, one raised so they're not all in one plane.

layouts.caption: gps-deploy: four bare computers with modems on top, one raised 6 blocks.

layouts.caption: One satellite from gps-deploy satellite: the computer inside a 3×3×3 iron hull, the modem in its top under an end-rod antenna and a slab dish, daylight-detector solar wings on iron bars, sea lanterns at the tips and underneath.

layouts.title: Satellite constellation
layouts.caption: gps-deploy satellite: the four satellites, 19 blocks apart, the fourth 9 higher.

programs.name: blueprint-projector
programs.title: Blueprint Projector
programs.tagline: Projects a building plan into the world as outlines: move and turn it from a monitor to see how it looks, then build it layer by layer.
features: Plans are JSON or Lua files in /plans: install more with install plan <name>, or write your own
Move, raise and turn the building from the monitor
Layer view outlines every block of one layer to build from
Top-down map of the layer, and the blocks it needs in three tabs: this layer, the whole build, and what the builder turtles are waiting for now
Follows a village turtle and projects the building it's working on
Tap Build and builder turtles build it right where it's shown, split between up to 4 of them
Builds in the sky too: the sky station plan is 63 wide, 98 high and built in the air
Or Turtle Works: a factory hall wired up under the floor, with docks for the turtles
setup: Place an advanced computer with a Spatial Projector beside it and an advanced monitor touching it.
Right-click the projector with Spatial Goggles to bind them, and wear them.
Install it, then a plan or two (install plan cottage), and reboot: the first plan appears 2 blocks south of the projector.
Tap the arrows on the monitor to pick a plan, then move it into place.
commands: show the last plan (startup does this)
a plan that takes a size: wide x long x high
follow what a village turtle is building
have the builder turtles (or instabuild) build the plan where it's shown (or tap Build)
load a plan and list the blocks it needs
integrates: 'projector village' shows the turtle's current building where it's building it, layer by layer.
Build sends the plan, in world coordinates, to a builder turtle; the panel follows its progress.
In creative, with instabuild serve running on a command computer, Build places the plan there in seconds instead.
Shows which plan is up, where it is and the layer you're on.
Optional: without lib/report.lua or a modem it just projects.

render.caption: The control panel on an advanced monitor. Tap the buttons: the map shows the current layer, north up.

programs.name: builder-turtle
programs.title: Builder
programs.tagline: Builds whatever the blueprint projector is showing, right where it's shown: tap Build and watch it go up layer by layer.
features: Clears the plot (not for a plan built in the air), then builds every layer from the block above it
Restocks from the supply chest behind its home, or orders from the storage system
Far from the storage cable? Its supply chest can be an ender chest whose twin is on the cable: no setup, just an ender modem on the turtle
Reports to the projector: the panel shows how far it's got and Layer view follows it
Several builders share one building, a strip each, crossing over at heights of their own
Saves after every block, so a reboot or chunk reload carries on where it stopped
Builds in real world coordinates from GPS, and waits for GPS before it moves
setup: Put the turtle on its home block with a wireless modem: supply chest behind it, spoil chest to its left, and (best with a big barrel) an empty buffer chest under it.
Run builder: it finds its position and facing with GPS. Reboot.

Fill the supply chest with the plan's blocks and coal (or put a wired modem on it, on the storage cable, and the storage system fills it; far away, make it an ender chest whose twin is on the cable), then tap Build on the projector.
commands: wait for a building from a projector (runs on boot)
what it's building and how far along
integrates: Sends it the plan when you tap Build, and shows its progress on the panel.
Orders each load of blocks and coal into its supply chest, which it tells the storage system is its own. Far away, the supply chest is an ender chest whose twin sits on the storage cable.
Needs GPS: it finds its own position and checks it as it builds.
All its moves go through lib/nav.lua, so chests and computers are never dug.

render.caption: The projector beside a half-built cottage, the builder placing the next layer, and its home with the supply and spoil chests.

programs.name: build-control
programs.title: Build Control
programs.deviceLabel: Any computer or pocket computer + wireless modem
programs.tagline: Sends a plan to the builder turtles at coordinates you type, no projector needed: from a pocket computer, build skystation 100 150 -40.
features: Any plan in /plans: install more with install plan <name>, or write your own JSON
Coordinates are the building's north-west bottom corner; turn it to face any way
build <plan> here uses the pocket computer's GPS position
Shows the box it fills and asks before anything is sent
Splits the building between the builders in range and follows them, as the projector does
Picks the build back up after a reboot, so waiting strips still get handed out
setup: Set up the builder turtles first, each on its home block with its chests.
Install this on any computer or pocket computer with a wireless or ender modem.
Install the plans you want: install plan <name> (install plans lists them; none come with it).
Run build <plan> <x> <y> <z> [facing], check the box it prints, and press y.
commands: the plans on this computer, with their sizes
its size and the blocks it needs
build it with its north-west bottom corner at x y z
the same, at this computer's GPS position
a plan that takes a size: wide x long x high
follow the builders (runs on boot while one is building)
call them off; again to give up on ones that don't answer
integrates: Each builder in range takes a strip of the building, as from the projector's Build button.
Reads the same plans; use it when you want to see and place the building first.
Shows how far the builders have got.

render.caption: On a pocket computer: the sky station sent to four builder turtles, then their progress as it changes.

programs.name: instabuild
programs.title: Instabuild
programs.tagline: Creative only: places a whole plan in seconds from a command computer, typed in or where the blueprint projector shows it, never replacing a block, and undoes it again.
features: Any plan in /plans, at the same coordinates and facing as build control
instabuild serve: tap Build on the blueprint projector and it places the plan where it's shown
Never replaces a block: plan blocks only go into air, and it says how many it left out
Keeps a list of what it placed: instabuild undo takes it out again
A row of the same block goes in with one fill
setup: In a creative world: /give @s computercraft:computer_command, and place it anywhere.
Install this on it, then the plans you want: install plan <name>.
Run instabuild <plan> <x> <y> <z> [facing], check the box it prints, and press y.
Or, with a modem: run instabuild serve, place the plan with the blueprint projector and tap Build there.
commands: the plans here, with their sizes
its size and the blocks it uses
build it with its north-west bottom corner at x y z
2 blocks south of this computer, on its level
a plan that takes a size: wide x long x high
place what the blueprint projector shows when Build is tapped on it (U undo, Q stop)
remove what the last build placed
integrates: Same plans and coordinates: try a spot with instabuild, undo, then have the turtles build it for real.
With instabuild serve running, the projector's Build places the plan exactly where it's shown.

render.caption: On a command computer: the sky station placed in one go, a run of the same block at a time.

programs.name: storage-computer
programs.title: Storage System
programs.tagline: Turns a wall of networked chests, or an AE2 or Refined Storage system, into one searchable store that every turtle can ask for items, and shows on a monitor where everything is going.
features: Type to search every chest at once (Delete clears it)
Enter sends a stack to the output chest, Right arrow just one

The monitor's network view: every ender chest and every turtle's and computer's chest it serves, how full each is and what's been sent to it in the last 5 minutes, red when one is full or gone, orange when items pile up
The requests waiting, the one being answered and the slowest lately, so a queue or a bottleneck shows at once
Items on the monitor too: sort, search on an on-screen keyboard, tap an item and send 1, 16 or 64 to the output chest
The monitor shows the smelter, enricher, crafters and every other service working with it, coloured by state, near or far away
Puts new items next to the same item when it can
Moves what you have most of into barrels with stack upgrades (Sophisticated Storage)
Turtles can ask for items over rednet; the village builder and builder stock themselves from it
Turtles find their own chest on the network: place one against a chest with a wired modem and its items go there
Only items, no recipes: the craft overseer plans and runs every craft, so a big modpack's recipes never slow down item requests
A fuel chest keeps the coal and charcoal for the smelter's furnaces and for turtles
Can use an AE2 or Refined Storage system (via an Advanced Peripherals bridge) instead of chests: turtles don't notice the difference
setup: Put a full-block wired modem against each chest (or small modems on barrels), a wired modem on the computer, and join them with cable. Right-click each modem.
For AE2 or Refined Storage: put an ME Bridge or RS Bridge against the system, with a wired modem on the same cable.

Run storage: the setup screen opens on the monitor and the computer. Tap (or click) the input and output chests, and any extra input, shared delivery, crafter, fuel and transfer chests, from lists that show what's in each chest; Save. Turtles' chests need no picking: they find their own. Reboot.
commands: start (opens the setup screen the first time)
the setup screen, on the monitor and the computer (in the running storage program, if there is one); or tap Setup at the top right of the monitor or screen, or press F1
change one setting by typing: input, inputs, output, delivery, crafter, fuel, transfer, remote (no setting: the setup screen)
list the turtles' chests, check deliveries, the fuel chest and the wireless modem, and say whether a craft overseer answers
show slot sizes and sort bulk items into storage with stack upgrades now
move everything stored into an ender chest whose twin is another storage system's input chest (stop: stop it)
integrates: Sends building blocks and coal to the village's supply chest as the builder needs them.
The recipe server: plans every craft from what's stored and has this computer load its crafting turtles' chests; with an ME or RS system, has the system craft from its patterns.
Its chest on the cable is loaded with each batch the craft overseer hands it.

Loads its furnaces, Mekanism and Create feeders and cooking pots when it asks (or fills its work chest in one go); what's made comes back through the input chest, charcoal into the fuel chest, botany pots' essence too.
Use its chest as the input and logs are put away as they arrive.
Keeps it stocked with a Creative Crate's item through the input chest.
Reports how many items and slots are in use, and each delivery.

render.caption: The storage terminal: type to search, Enter for a stack. Click a row, and the row again to take a stack.

more.caption: The monitor's network view (where it starts): every ender chest and turtle's or computer's chest the storage system feeds, its slots in use and what's been sent to it (>) or taken from it (<) in the last 5 minutes. The remote terminal's ender chest is piling up (orange) and a builder's chest is full (red); the line above shows the requests waiting. Tap a row for what's in it.

The monitor's Items view (an advanced monitor, for touch; Network at the top goes back to the network view): Most / A-Z sorts, Find opens the on-screen keyboard, the arrows turn the page. Tap an item, then how many to send to the output chest. Click to try it.

Setup opens the setup screen on the monitor (and on the computer): every setting on one page; tap one for every chest on the network with what's in it, a page at a time, Empty for empty ones only. Click to try it.

programs.name: remote-terminal
programs.title: Remote Terminal
programs.tagline: The storage system from anywhere, through a linked ender chest: search what's stored and pull it, or drop items in to send them home.
features: Type to search everything stored; Enter pulls a stack, Right pulls one
Items arrive in the ender chest next to it, from its twin on the storage cable at home
Drop anything in the ender chest to send it home into storage
Asks for anything that isn't stored but can be crafted, like a turtle's order
Finds its chest's twin at home by itself: nothing to pick in storage setup
remote get 64 iron ingot pulls from the command line
setup: Update the storage computer and give it an ender modem.
Put an ender chest on the storage cable at home with a wired modem, and its twin (same colours) next to this computer.
Put an ender modem on this computer, install and reboot.
commands: pull 64 of the first stored item matching the text
pick the ender chest when it can see more than one
integrates: Lists what's stored, sends what's asked for into the home ender chest and puts away whatever else turns up in it.
Tells the storage computer which chest at home is the twin of this one.
Crafts what's asked for but not stored.
Shows how many kinds of item are stored and each pull.

render.caption: The remote terminal: search what's stored at home and pull it through the ender chest.

programs.name: craft-terminal
programs.title: Craft Terminal
programs.tagline: A computer just for ordering crafts: everything the storage system can make, with how many, made into a chest next to it or into storage.
features: Lists everything the storage system can craft from what's stored, A to Z, with how many it could make and how many are stored
Type to search; Enter asks how many (a stack to start), Right orders one
Crafts come to a chest next to it as they're made, or stay in storage (Tab switches)
Shows what's being crafted right now, or why crafting is stuck
The craft overseer works out the list and makes the orders: with the crafting turtles, the factory's infusers and an ME or RS system's patterns
Finds its chest by itself: nothing to pick in storage setup
crafts make 64 torch orders from the command line
setup: Run a craft overseer (computers/craft-overseer): it has the recipes and makes the orders.
Put this computer by the storage system with a wired modem on the storage cable (right-click it red).
Optional: a chest touching it with a full-block wired modem on the same cable, for the crafts to come to.
Install and reboot.
commands: craft 64 of the first craftable item matching the text
pick the chest crafts go to, from a list
keep crafts in storage, even with a chest next to it
integrates: Works out what can be crafted while a craft terminal is running, plans each order and has what's made sent to the terminal's chest.
Sends what's made into the terminal's chest when the overseer says.
Tells the storage computer which chest is this terminal's.
The other half: search and take what's stored. This one is for having things made.
Shows how many things can be crafted and each order.

render.caption: The craft terminal: search what can be made, say how many, and it's crafted into the chest next to it.

lines: Crafting 16 Chest: it comes to the chest.

programs.name: cannon-feeder
programs.title: Cannon Feeder
programs.tagline: Keeps a Create Schematicannon stocked from the storage system: with a Block Reader on the cannon it sends whatever the cannon is waiting for, or give it the material list; what's missing is crafted on the way.
features: With an Advanced Peripherals Block Reader on the cannon, sends the item it's waiting for at once and keeps it topped up until the cannon finishes
Keeps the chest touching the cannon topped up with everything on its list, until all of each is sent and never more
List from typed items (cannon add stone_bricks 340) or every block a plan from /plans uses
Crafts what storage hasn't got but can make, with the crafting turtles or the craft overseer
Keeps gunpowder in the chest for the cannon while there's more to send
Screen leads with what's missing now: the item the cannon is stuck on and why, and every item storage can't send enough of; tap for what has been sent
Near the storage on its cable, or anywhere through an ender chest
setup: Put a chest against the Schematicannon and this computer against the chest.
Join the chest to the storage cable with a wired modem, or make it an ender chest whose twin is on the storage cable (ender modems on both computers).
Put a Block Reader against the cannon, facing it, touching this computer: it sends what the cannon asks for. Or type the cannon's material list with cannon add.
Install and reboot.
commands: add an item and how many to the list
take an item off the list
add every block a plan from /plans uses
the list, and how much of each is sent
pick the chest, if it touches more than one
integrates: Sends what's on the list into the chest by the cannon, and crafts what it hasn't got.
Tells the storage computer which chest is the one by the cannon.
Crafts what's missing, across all the crafting turtles.
Shows how many items are still to send.

render.caption: The feeder's screen with a Block Reader on the cannon: what's missing now comes first. The cannon waits for mossy walls while they're crafted, then for lanterns, which need iron nuggets storage hasn't got; the bottom line is what has been sent. Tap for the Sent page.

lines: Added 6 kinds of block from cottage.

programs.name: crafter-turtle
programs.title: Crafter
programs.tagline: The storage system's crafting arm: makes what turtles ask for but isn't stored, from what is, ingredients first.
features: Plans whole chains: logs into planks into sticks into fences
Knows everything craftable the village themes use
Teach it any recipe by laying it out in its grid
Never crafts an order twice while it's being made
setup: A crafty turtle with a wireless modem, and a chest directly in front of it.
Connect the chest to the storage network with a full-block wired modem.
Install and reboot the turtle: it tells the storage computer that chest is the crafter chest, so there's nothing to pick in storage setup.
commands: teach the craft overseer the recipe laid out in the grid
integrates: Plans the crafts (it has the recipes) and hands each crafting turtle its share of the jobs.
Loads the ingredients into the crafter chest when the overseer asks.
On an essence farm (botany pots far away), the farm finds its barrel and hands it the jobs from its own essence.
Fences, slabs, beds and lanterns get made as the village builder asks for them.

render.caption: The storage wall and its computer, and the crafty turtle with its chest, all on one wired network.

programs.name: craft-overseer
programs.title: Craft Overseer
programs.tagline: The storage system's recipe server: knows every recipe (your modpack's too), plans every craft and shares it between any number of crafting turtles, with the queue and what each job is missing on a monitor.
features: Knows every crafting recipe in your modpack, not just vanilla (tools/recipes.mjs), and recipes taught with crafter learn
Plans whole chains from what's stored (logs into planks into sticks into fences) and hands each job to a free crafting turtle
Answers every program's crafting questions: builders, the village builder, the cannon feeder and the factory ask it what can be made and have it made
Works out the craft terminal's list and sends its orders to the terminal's chest
The factory's infusers and essence farm run the steps only they can make
Steps of one order run in turn; different orders run side by side
Monitor lists every turtle, the queue, and what each job is short of
Moves a job to another turtle when one stops answering
Far from the storage system: one pair of ender chests for every crafting turtle, each batch passed on to the turtle's barrel
Keeps its queue across reboots
setup: Put an advanced computer on the storage cable with a wired modem, and a wireless or ender modem so turtles and far-away computers can ask it about crafting. A monitor is optional.
Set up crafting turtles, each with its own chest in front of it on the storage cable.
With a modpack: put its pack_recipes.lua on this computer (not the storage computer).
Install and reboot.
Far away: an ender chest on its own cable (the twin on the storage cable), each turtle's barrel on that cable too, an ender modem, then overseer hub.
commands: use the ender chest on its cable for crafting turtles far from the storage system
integrates: Counts what's stored for its plans and loads each turtle's chest when the overseer asks; with an ME or RS system, crafts from its patterns.
How every other program asks it what could be made and has it made.
Gets its list of what can be crafted from it, and orders.
Its infusers and essence farm tell it what they can make and run those steps of its plans.
Each crafting turtle takes the batches it's given; add more for more crafting at once.
Shows how many jobs are queued.

render.caption: The overseer's monitor: three crafting turtles working through the queue; the lantern waits for iron nuggets. Click to add an order.

programs.name: factory
programs.title: Factory
programs.tagline: Every machine that turns stored items into something else, whatever your mods: furnaces, Mekanism smelters, enrichment chambers and infusers, Create crushers, washers and fans, Cobblemon cooking pots and Mystical Agriculture botany pots. One program, on as many computers as you like.
stats: vanilla, Mekanism, Create, Cobblemon, Mystical Agriculture
features: Furnaces, blast furnaces and smokers: ores, dust and food smelted and cooked, fuelled from the fuel chest; charcoal, stone and glass on order
Mekanism Enrichment Chambers (2 dust per ore block, 4 per 3 raw ores) and Energized Smelters, fed through a hopper or barrel

Mekanism Metallurgic Infusers on request: steel, alloys, circuits, bronze and more, from +1 / +8 / +64 buttons on the Infuser tab or the monitor; the storage computer orders the infusing its crafts need, and a missing in-between step (enriched iron for steel) is made first
Create crushing wheels, washing fans (crushed ores into nuggets and a byproduct, crafted back into ingots) and blasting and smoking fans: no Mekanism needed

Cobblemon cooking pots: exp candy from sculk and honeycomb, compressed up to XL, read through a comparator so a pot never jams; sculk and honeycomb crafted to keep them coming, when the storage system has recipes; a Candy page on the monitor

Hopper Botany Pots of Mystical Agriculture essence emptied into storage, and a recipe finder that orders what the essence crafts into; far away an essence farm that keeps its essence and crafts what the storage computer asks for with its own turtles
Runs only what it finds or you add: Create only, furnaces only or everything, with one program
Several factory computers share a cable: each furnace and botany pot belongs to one, and smelters leave the ores an enricher anywhere takes; the Chain page shows what happens where
One setup screen for everything: found machines and whose they are, + Add rows for each kind, output chests picked by dropping an item in
Optional work chest (one request a round), or far away through an ender chest; a tab per part on the computer, a tile per machine on the monitor
Replaces the smelter, enricher, cooker and essence computers: they update to it by themselves and keep their setup
setup: Set up the storage system first (install update it if it's older than the factory). Put wired modems on your furnaces and on the hoppers, barrels and chests that feed and empty your other machines, joined to the storage cable.

Place this computer on the same cable with a wired modem (and a monitor if you like), install and reboot. Furnaces and botany pots are found by themselves (pots that empty into a barrel: add the barrel as a pot barrel).

Open the setup screen (Setup on the monitor or screen, F1, or factory setup) and add the rest under Machines: Mekanism machines (an infuser has two feeders: one on top, one at the side), Create lines and cooking pots. Pick a work chest if you have many machines.
commands: the setup screen on the monitor and the computer: machines, the chain, the work chest, the monitor; or tap Setup, or press F1
add a machine: chamber, smelter, infuser (Mekanism), crusher, washer, fan, smokefan (Create), pot (Cobblemon) or potbarrel (the barrel botany pots empty into)
every machine added here, and the furnaces and botany pots found and whose they are
hand this computer's furnaces and botany pots to factory computer 14
make 256 charcoal from spruce logs (also stone, glass and cancel)
ask the infusers for 64 steel dust (factory infuse lists the recipes; factory infuse cancel cancels)
essence recipes for anything with iron in its name, and how many you can make
order 64 iron ingots made from essence
pick the work chest (none: stop using one; remote: far away through an ender chest)
pick the monitor for the status board
integrates: Holds everything, loads the furnaces, feeders and pot hoppers (or fills the work chest in one go), and takes back what's made through its input chest; crafts washed nuggets and essence orders.
One request a round fills the work chest with every furnace's and feeder's load and fuel.
Reads the Mekanism machines, Create lines and their feeders, sets the machines' sides and tells the storage computer which barrels are feeders.
Crafts the washers' nuggets back into ingots, and the essence orders; on an essence farm, its own turtles do.
Digital Miners with silk touch fill storage with ore blocks: 2 ingots each through the chambers.
Its logs pile up in storage: burn the spare ones into charcoal.
Shows what each factory computer is doing, and when a machine needs attention.

render.caption: The Smelter tab: every furnace, what's in it and its fuel. Click the footer to place a charcoal, stone or glass order.

more.caption: The monitor is a status board: a tile per machine (smaller tiles when there are many, so every machine fits), lime idle, yellow working, orange flat out, red when it needs you (no fuel or power, output stuck, a Create line not moving, a pot not cooking).
The Enricher tab: each chamber, crusher and washer, the ore it's on, how many are queued in it and its feeder, its power and what it's doing.
The Infuser tab: each recipe, how many you can make from what is stored, and buttons to ask for more; what is asked for is listed under it (the storage computer orders too). Try the buttons.
The Cooking tab: each cooking pot, what it makes, how many it has made and what it's doing.
The monitor's Candy page: each size in storage and in the pots, the exp it's worth, and what's left to make more XS from.
The Essence tab: what the stored essence makes, how many you can make, and an order of 4 crafts of iron ingots.

Builder work orders and whether a builder has taken them
Red title bar, speaker alarm and status-server alert during raids

Pauses the reactor while the Induction Matrix is full and starts it again when there's room

Put an advanced monitor next to the computer, then install and reboot.

libraries.name: nav
libraries.title: lib/nav
libraries.tagline: Turtle position tracking and safe movement. Saved after every move, corrected by GPS, never digs your chests.
libraries.usage:
local nav = require("lib.nav")

if not nav.init() then            -- loads saved position, calibrates with GPS
  nav.setPosition(0, 0, 0, "north")
end

local ok, err = nav.forward()     -- digs through anything that isn't protected
if not ok then print("Stuck: " .. err) end

nav.goTo(10, 64, -5)              -- rises first, then x, then z, then down
nav.writeFile("/.myjob_job", job) -- crash-safe state file
api: Load the saved position; calibrate with GPS unless useGps is false. Returns true if the position is known.
Wait until GPS answers (moving turtles need it), saying why on screen and on the status server. Returns { x, y, z }.
Set position and heading outright (h is 0-3 or north/east/south/west).
Move, digging whatever is in the way. Returns ok, err (nofuel, protected, bedrock, undiggable, blocked).
Turn; face picks the shortest way round.
Clear the block above or below, waiting out falling gravel.
Travel: rise to y, then x, then z, then descend. Climbs and retries if blocked.
Current position { x, y, z } and heading 0-3.
Crash-safe state files (temp file, then move).
How far it may go from where it started (set nav.range 64; 256 unless set, 0 for no limit), that start, and whether a column is in reach: a forward move past it returns false, nav.TOO_FAR.
libraries.notes: Headings: 0 north (-z), 1 east (+x), 2 south (+z), 3 west (-x). Never dug: chests, barrels, shulker boxes, hoppers, furnaces, spawners and anything from ComputerCraft. A turtle never goes more than nav.range blocks (256 unless set) along X or Z from where it started; up and down always work.

libraries.name: report
libraries.title: lib/report
libraries.tagline: Put any computer on the status dashboard with a few lines. Does nothing without a modem, so it's always safe to include.
libraries.usage:
local report = require("lib.report")
report.init("wheat farm")              -- what this computer is for

local function main()
  report.set("harvesting", "row 3 of 8") -- state + what it's doing
  report.log("chest full")              -- a line in its activity list
end

parallel.waitForAny(main, report.loop) -- keeps it online while main runs
api: Say what this computer is for, e.g. "auto miner". Call once.
Current state and what it's doing. Cheap: only sends on change or as a heartbeat.
A one-off line for the computer's activity list.
Heartbeat loop. Run it beside your program with parallel.
libraries.notes: States are one lowercase word. The dashboard colours them: green working, grey idle, yellow/orange waiting or paused, blue travelling, red error. Pass { pos = { x, y, z } } in extra if the program tracks its own position.

libraries.name: errlog
libraries.title: lib/errlog
libraries.tagline: Every program saves its errors to /errors.log in the same format, so you can see what went wrong after the screen has moved on.
libraries.usage:
local errlog = require("lib.errlog")
errlog.init("excavate", function() return { pos = nav.getPos() } end)

local ok, err = errlog.pcall(run)       -- pcall that logs the error + stack trace
errlog.error("chest missing", { slot = 3 }) -- an error you caught yourself
errlog.warn("fuel low")                  -- worth knowing, not fatal
api: Name entries are filed under, and an optional function returning fields added to every entry (position, job).
Drop-in pcall that logs the error with a stack trace before returning it.
Log an error you caught yourself, with optional extra fields.
Log something worth knowing that isn't fatal.
The newest n entries (default 5) as strings.
libraries.notes: Each entry: [real time | game day and time] LEVEL program (label #id), then the message, the fields, fuel on turtles and the stack trace, indented, with a blank line after. The same error within a minute is counted instead of written again, Ctrl+T is never logged, and the file is trimmed to its newest 8 KB once it passes 16 KB. Read it in-game with edit /errors.log.

libraries.name: claim
libraries.title: lib/claim
libraries.tagline: Place a turtle against a chest on the storage network and it tells the storage computer that chest is its own. Nothing to pick in storage setup.
libraries.usage:
local claim = require("lib.claim")

-- askStorage(msg): your request function on the "storage" protocol
local ok, chest = claim.chest(askStorage, "delivery", "front")
if ok then
  print("Deliveries go to " .. chest)
elseif ok == false then
  print("Couldn't hook my chest up: " .. chest)
end -- nil: no storage system answered
api: Tell the storage computer the chest on that side is mine. role is "delivery" (my orders go there) or "crafter". Returns true and the chest's network name, false and why not, or nil if nothing answered.
libraries.notes: The turtle sends what's in its chest. If that's the chest the storage computer already has for it, it answers at once; otherwise it drops one item into each chest that could be it until the turtle sees it arrive, and takes it back each time. The storage system needs at least one item in it. The chest needs a wired modem on the storage cable.

libraries.name: mekfeed
libraries.title: lib/mekfeed
libraries.tagline: Mekanism machines fed through a hopper or barrel (CC can't reach their slots): reads them and their feeders at once, sets their output side, registers barrel feeders with the storage computer and handles the add / remove commands. Also Create lines (crushing wheels, fans), which CC can't see at all: a feeder chest and an output chest.
libraries.usage:
local mekfeed = require("lib.mekfeed")

local set = mekfeed.new({ name = "smelter", single = "energizedSmelter",
  factory = "SmeltingFactory", what = "energized smelter", title = "Smelter",
  ask = ask, tell = tell })

-- each round:
local machines = set:read()
local unsure = set:register(work.remote)
set:unstick(machines, input, function(m, item) end)
for _, m in ipairs(machines) do
  if mekfeed.ready(m) and not unsure[m.entry.feeder] then
    local n = mekfeed.space(m, "minecraft:raw_iron")
    -- send n into m.entry.feeder, then mekfeed.added(m, name, sent)
  end
end
api: A set of machines saved in /.<name>_machines: single and factory are the peripheral types (factory a suffix after the tier), what / title for messages, names, setSides, ask, tell; lines = { "crush", "wash" } or { "blast", "smoke" } adds Create lines (kinds in mekfeed.LINES), pageTitle names the setup page. For the infuser: extra = { title, hint } (a second feeder each, for the extra slot), sides (the side config to set), read(m, call) (more reads per machine), needOutput (an output chest must be picked).

Every saved machine and its feeder, read side by side (each Mekanism call takes a tick), sides set once. Each: entry { machine, feeder }, title, slots, factory, present, inputs, outputs, energy, usage, feedOk, feedSize, feedList, feed, feedTotal.
Tells the storage computer which barrels and chests are feeders ('feeders'). The feeders not to fill yet (name -> true) and why.
The same for several sets on one computer at once (the factory's smelter, enricher and infuser): the storage computer keeps one feeder list per computer, and each 'feeders' replaces it.
An item sitting in a feeder over an empty, powered machine for a minute goes back to input; putBack(m, item) is told.

Empties each machine's output chest into input (the storage input chest, or far away the ender chest). How many moved, true if some didn't fit, why a move failed, and item -> how many of it moved (the smelter counts its orders with it).

Status board colour and words: red (not on network, no feeder or output chest, no power, output full; a Create line: not moving), orange (working flat out: every slot busy and a stack waiting), yellow (working: says working), lime (idle).
Present, powered and its feeder answers.
The most of an item its feeder may be sent: room in the machine's input slots less what's waiting, and room in the feeder.
What's in its feeder, or in a single machine's slot: keep sending that. nil when it's free.
Note the feeder was sent n.
'<program> add [machine feeder [output]]' (machine may be a Create line's word: crusher, washer, fan, smokefan) and 'remove <n>'; false if args is neither.
The setup page's rows, for a page of your own: parts.entries() (a row per machine, tap to change it), parts.adds() (the + Add rows), parts.add(line). set:setupPage(ui) puts them on one page.
Every peripheral its machines use; the machines on the network not added yet (here or, with opts.taken, by another computer).
libraries.notes: The machine ejects what it makes out of its bottom into its output chest (emptied by collect, registered like a barrel feeder) or a storage input chest: read sets that side to Output with Auto-eject when the machine is Public. A barrel feeder needs something moving its items into the machine (a logistical transporter set to pull, a funnel), has to be empty when added, and isn't filled until the storage computer has taken it as a feeder (it stops being storage). Far away (remote) nothing is registered.

libraries.name: setupui
libraries.title: lib/setupui
libraries.tagline: Setup screens on the monitor and the terminal at once: pages of settings, and chest lists a page at a time with what's in each chest, an Empty filter and typed search. The storage computer's, the enricher's, the smelter's, the cooker's and the essence computer's setup screens are built on it.
libraries.usage:
local setupui = require("lib.setupui")

local ui = setupui.new({ screens = { termScreen, monScreen } })
local saved = ui:run({
  title = "Storage settings",
  rows = function(ui) return { { label = "Fuel chest", value = fuel or "none",
    act = function() ui:pickChest({ title = "Pick: Fuel chest", names = names, none = "(none)",
      pick = function(name) fuel = name; ui:back() end }) end } } end,
  buttons = function(ui) return { { " Save ", "black", "lime", function() ui:finish(true) end } } end,
})
api: A setup screen drawn on every lib/screen.lua screen given (the first is the terminal: the keyboard moves its highlight). onEvent sees every event.

Shows page until ui:finish(result); returns result. A page has title, hint, rows(ui) -> { { label, value, colour, labelColour, dim, act } }, optional buttons(ui), filter (typing narrows it), empty(row) (an Empty button).
Go to a page, and back to the one before.
The message line; draw now (before a slow call).
A page of chests (o.names) with what's in each; o.pick(name) when one is tapped, o.none adds a (none) row, o.roleOf greys out used ones, o.only leaves some out.

Like pickChest, but the player drops any item into the chest they mean: every empty one of o.names is watched (page.tick, once a second) and the first to get something is o.pick(name); o.list() shows a plain list instead.
Pick the monitor a lib/screen.lua setting names, and queue event.
name -> { stacks, top }: every chest's contents, read at once (each call takes a tick otherwise).
libraries.notes: Rows past the screen's height go on more pages (the < > buttons, Page Up / Down, the mouse wheel). Every chest's contents are read side by side when a list opens, so even hundreds of chests show at once.

libraries.name: workchest
libraries.title: lib/workchest
libraries.tagline: A computer's work chest: the storage computer fills it in one request a round, and the program loads its own furnaces or hoppers from it, on the storage cable or far away through ender chests.
libraries.usage:
local workchest = require("lib.workchest")

-- ask(msg): your request function on the "storage" protocol
local work = workchest.new("smelter", ask)

-- each round, after asking for 'stock':
local input = work:input(stock.input) -- far away: the ender chest itself (or the return one)
if work:check(stock) or work.remote then
  work:fill({ ["minecraft:raw_iron"] = 64 }, 64) -- items, and fuel for 64 smelts
  work:move("minecraft:raw_iron", "minecraft:furnace_2", 1, 64)
  work:move("minecraft:coal", "minecraft:furnace_2", 2, 8)
  work:empty(input) -- the rest back into storage
else
  -- no work chest (work.problem says why): 'send' to each furnace
end
api: A work chest for this program; the chest's name is saved in /.<name>_chest.

Far away: chest is the ender chest here; back (optional) a return one whose twin is a storage input chest. Without back, things go home through chest: each fill sweeps out what wasn't asked for. The storage computer finds the chest's twin by probe. Same answers as set.
Where finished items go back: far away the ender chest itself (the next fill sweeps them home) or the return chest, else the storage input chest.
Make this empty chest the work chest (nil: stop using one; its contents go back). True, false and why, or nil if nothing answered.
After each 'stock' reply: true while the work chest is in use. Claims the saved one again if the storage computer forgot it (once a minute); work.problem says why not.
Top it up to items (name -> n) and fuel for that many smelts, in one request; with one ender chest both ways it asks every round and first sends home what wasn't asked for. The reply, or nil and why.
Move up to n of an item from it into a furnace or hopper (slot optional). How many went.
Send everything left back through the storage input chest.
The '<program> chest [name|none|remote]' command: pick, name, set up far away or drop the work chest, printing how it went.
libraries.notes: Only an empty chest can become a work chest, so a storage chest full of items is never taken, and it stops being storage. The storage computer keeps it across 'storage setup' and while it's missing. Whatever is left at the end of a round goes back through the input chest, so items never sit there unseen. A storage computer too old to know work chests never answers 'work', and the program carries on with 'send'. Far away (an EnderStorage-style ender chest pair, or two, and an ender modem) there is no 'send' to fall back on: nothing is loaded until the work chest is back in use (check with work.remote).

libraries.name: net
libraries.title: lib/net
libraries.tagline: Rednet the same way in every program: ask another computer something and get its answer (never a stale one, never waiting forever), answer, and find who hosts a protocol.
libraries.usage:
local net = require("lib.net")

local storage = net.peer("storage", { retry = 60 })
local reply, why = storage:ask({ type = "count", items = { "minecraft:torch" } })
if not reply then print("No storage system: " .. why) end

-- the other side
local from, msg = rednet.receive("storage")
net.answer(from, "storage", msg, { counts = counts })
api: Open wireless and ender modems, or every modem with "any". True if rednet is open. Just after boot it waits up to 15 s for a modem to attach.
Run beside the program (parallel): opens modems that attach after it started.
Send msg with a fresh id and wait for the answer that repeats it. opts: wait (seconds), match(reply), other(from, msg) for anything else that arrives.
Answer a request: adds re (its type) and its id.

The computer hosting a protocol, looked up once and remembered until it goes quiet. opts: open, retry, wait, host. For 5 minutes after boot a missing peer is looked for every 5 s, whatever retry says.
Ask it something: the answer, or nil and why ("no modem", "none" or "no answer").
A wireless or ender modem is attached.
libraries.notes: Every request carries an id that the answer repeats, along with re (the request type), so a late answer to an earlier request is never taken for a newer one. Ids come from one counter per computer, so several parts of a program can ask at once. Protocols that answer differently (a builder's accepted / busy, a crafter's crafted) pass match.

libraries.name: crafts
libraries.title: lib/crafts
libraries.tagline: Crafting questions for the craft overseer, the storage system's recipe server: what could be made, and having it made, added to the storage computer's answers.
libraries.usage:
local crafts = require("lib.crafts")

local r = storage:ask({ type = "deliver", items = want })
crafts.deliver(r, want)      -- r.crafting, r.cantCraft for what's short

local c = storage:ask({ type = "count", items = names })
crafts.count(c, names, need) -- c.craftable
api: After a storage computer's deliver reply: has what didn't arrive and isn't stored made, and adds crafting, cantCraft and craftProblem to r.
After a count reply: adds r.craftable, how many more of each could be made (being made included).
Start crafting so there'll be n of each in all: { crafting, cantCraft, craftProblem }.
Anything else on the craft_overseer protocol (craftable, craft, learn, recipes, makes, jobdone): the answer, or nil and why.
libraries.notes: The storage computer only keeps items and knows no recipes, so a modpack's thousands of them never slow down its answers. With no overseer running, every answer says so (cantCraft is "no craft overseer answered") and the program carries on with what's stored.

libraries.name: files
libraries.title: lib/files
libraries.tagline: Crash-safe save files: a table goes to a temp file first, then into place, so a crash or chunk unload never leaves a broken file.
libraries.usage:
local files = require("lib.files")

files.write("/.myjob_job", job)
local job = files.read("/.myjob_job") -- nil if there's none
files.delete("/.myjob_job")
api: Serialise value to path through a temp file.
The saved value, from the temp copy if the move never happened; nil if there's none.
Remove the file and its temp copy.
libraries.notes: lib/nav.lua's writeFile, readFile and deleteFile are these same functions, so every turtle program installs this too.

libraries.name: inv
libraries.title: lib/inv
libraries.tagline: A turtle's inventory and fuel: count or pick an item, see how much room is left, and refuel from what's on board.
libraries.usage:
local inv = require("lib.inv")
local FUEL = { ["minecraft:coal"] = true, ["minecraft:charcoal"] = true }

if inv.fuelLevel() < 500 then inv.refuel(2000, FUEL) end
if inv.select("minecraft:torch") then turtle.placeDown() end
print(inv.emptySlots() .. " slots free")
api: How many matching items are on board.
Select the first slot holding one; false if there's none.
The fuel level, with "unlimited" as math.huge.
Burn items up to the target level: only fuels if given, else anything that burns.
libraries.notes: match is an item name, a list of names, a set like { ["minecraft:coal"] = true }, or a function of the item's name.

libraries.name: screen
libraries.title: lib/screen
libraries.tagline: Flicker-free monitors and terminals: each frame is drawn hidden and shown in one go, and frames that haven't changed are skipped.
libraries.usage:
local screen = require("lib.screen")
local s = screen.find({ scales = { 1, 0.5 }, minW = 40, fallback = term.current() })

if not s:same(key) then             -- optional: skip a frame that looks the same
  local win, w, h = s:frame()       -- hidden and cleared
  screen.put(win, 1, 1, "Hello", "yellow", "gray")
  s:show()                          -- up it goes, all at once
end
api: screen.tiles(t, w, top, bottom, tiles, minW)

A status board: a coloured tile per { title, text, bg, fg } between rows top and bottom: 3 rows high, else 2, else 1 (title: text), whichever shows them all, at least minW wide, stretched to fill. How many didn't fit even at 1 row.
What the tile colours mean on one row, { colour, word } pairs; stops before one that doesn't fit.

A screen on a monitor it finds itself: name (only that one), filter(name, monitor), scales (largest text that fits minW x minH, set once), fallback (e.g. term.current()) while there's no monitor, setting (a settings key, e.g. 'smelter.monitor', the player sets to a monitor's name or 'none'); unset, a monitor touching the computer first, else the first on the cable.

For a '<program> monitor' command: lists every monitor the computer sees (touching it or on the cable), saves the player's pick (or 'none', or arg given on the command line) in setting and returns it; nil when left as it was. Queue an event the running program calls refresh() on, so it moves straight away.
Call on peripheral / peripheral_detach: keeps a monitor that's still there, else moves to another or the fallback. True when it moved.
x, y (and true for a drag) when the event is a tap on its monitor, or a click while it's on the terminal.
What it draws on now (nil: nothing to draw on), and the monitor's name (nil on the terminal).
Wrap the terminal (term.current()) or a fixed target.
A hidden, cleared window the size of the screen to draw the next frame in, and its width and height. Made again when the screen is resized.
Show the frame in one go. Set the cursor on the window first if it should blink somewhere.
True when key matches the last frame at this size, so drawing can be skipped.
Draw on another monitor from now on.
screen.put(t, x, y, text, fg, bg)
Write text in colours: names ("lime") or numbers (colors.lime); bg is black if left out.
Cut or pad text to exactly w characters.
Cut text to at most w characters by taking out its middle (terracotta_h..pot_0), so a peripheral name keeps the number that tells it apart.
libraries.notes: Clearing a monitor and redrawing it in place makes it flash, so every program with a screen draws through this. Skipping unchanged frames also saves sending them to every player who can see the monitor. Turtles driving past fire peripheral events, so refresh() never rescales a monitor that is still there: rescaling is what flashes it. Every computer on a wired network sees every monitor on it, so each program passes a setting and the player can give it its own ('set storage.monitor monitor_3').

libraries.name: plan
libraries.title: lib/plan
libraries.tagline: Building plans: load a .json or .lua plan from /plans and place it in the world, turned to face any way.
libraries.usage:
local plan = require("lib.plan")

local p = assert(plan.load("skystation"))   -- /plans/skystation.json or .lua
local at = plan.corner(p, 0, 100, 150, -40) -- north-west bottom corner, facing north
local mats, blocks = plan.world(p, at)     -- names; { x, y, z, m } in world coords
print(p.name, p.w, p.l, p.h, #blocks)
api: The plan in /plans/<id>.json or .lua (or a file path), or nil and what's wrong with it: { name, mats, blocks, layers, w, l, h, clear }. A Lua plan gets opts as its "...".
Picks a plan's options out of a command's words, and returns them and the other words: a size like 31x25 or 31x25x8 is opts.size, key=value is opts[key].
Copy the plan's file to to plus its extension and return the new path: build from the copy so an update to /plans can't change a building half way.
A plan from a table already in memory (legend + layers, or a block list).
Where it goes ("at") so its north-west bottom corner is x y z, turned turn quarter turns clockwise.
Block names (facing states, and the sides of walls, fences and panes, turned with the plan), and every block as { x, y, z, m } in world coordinates.
A block name without its [state], and its facing as a heading (0 north .. 3 west) or nil.
The box it fills, and the ground it covers.
A plan block's offset from at, turned.
libraries.notes: A plan file is JSON (legend + layers, each layer rows of letters seen from above with the first row north; or blocks: [[x, y, z, "minecraft:stone"], ...]) or a Lua file returning the same table, for plans made by code. "clear": false marks one built in the air, so builders don't dig out its box first. A block can carry a state, "minecraft:spruce_stairs[facing=east]": builders face that way to place it, and turning the plan turns it (and north=tall style sides of walls and fences). A Lua plan can take options typed after the command, as its "...": the platform plan reads opts.size, so 'build platform 100 64 -20 north 31x25x8' builds it 31 by 25 and 8 high.

libraries.name: crew
libraries.title: lib/crew
libraries.tagline: Hands a building to the builder turtles in strips, follows them, gives waiting strips to the next free one, and stops them.
libraries.usage:
local crew = require("lib.crew")
local c = crew.new({
  job = function() return { id = id, name = p.name, mats = mats, blocks = blocks, area = area, clear = p.clear } end,
  build = saved.build, save = function(build) saved.build = build end,
  tell = print,
})
c:start()
parallel.waitForAny(function() c:run() end, other)
api: job() (the building in world coords), build (saved progress), save(build), tell(text), optional changed() and finished(text).
Split the job between the builders in range (up to 4, busy ones too: their strips wait); call them off (twice gives up on silent ones). Or queue crew.START / crew.STOP.
The loop: hears progress and hands out strips still waiting. Run it alongside the rest.
The build in progress (nil when done), a line on how it's going, and the lowest layer being built.
A line saying what the builders are stuck waiting for, added up over every builder ("Waiting for stone bricks (64), tuff (20)"), or nil.
libraries.notes: Talks to builder turtles on the projector_build protocol. The blueprint projector and build-control both use it, so a building goes up the same way from either.
